title: An ideal binary tree and a tree reduced to a chain
summary: The same seven nodes produce different heights depending on whether they branch or connect in a single chain.
description: The left panel is labeled “Ideal structure” and “Perfect binary tree.” Root 1 has left and right children 2 and 3, node 2 has children 4 and 5, and node 3 has children 6 and 7. All 4 bottom nodes, 4, 5, 6, and 7, are leaves. The tree has 3 levels. From root 1 to any leaf there are 2 edges, so its height is 2.

The right panel is labeled “Degenerate structure” and “Linked list.” All 7 nodes lean left in the chain 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7. Every right link is empty. There are 7 levels and 6 edges from root 1 to the only leaf 7, giving height 6.

frames.title: An ideal binary tree and a tree reduced to a chain
frames.explanation: When all levels are full, a perfect binary tree has minimum height and can exploit divide and conquer. A tree that degenerates into a one-sided linked list reaches maximum height and operations along a path can take linear time.
